newsitem.title: UK: Biocompatibles sets buy, share issue.
newsitem.headline: Biocompatibles sets buy, share issue.

text.p: British biotechnology company Biocompatibles Plc said on Tuesday it had acquired advanced stent technology to allow it to speed up its entry into what it believes to be a growing $1.0 billion market.

It said it had sealed a worldwide licence, through a new 60 percent-owned joint venture, to develop, manufacture and market stents -- surgery products -- based on designs by the Divysios company using Biocompatibles' phosphorylcholine coating.
The UK company will pay an initial $14 million. Divysios will use the cash to subscribe for new Biocompatible shares within a 45 million stg issue.
Divysio Solutions Ltd is a Canadian-based stent development company, which owns the rights to its stents.

"The Divysio transaction fulfils Biocompatibles' corporate objectives by accelerating our entry into the dynamic cardiovascular stent market with innovative products which have considerable potential," the statement quoted chief executive and president Alistair Taylor as saying.
An existing development agreement with Cordis for pc-coated stents will continue alongside the new Divysio pact, it added.

Biocompatibles said it would release details of its proposed equity fundraising "in due course", but in the first instance intended the payment mechanism with Divysio to be a way in which its new partner would become an owner of some of the new shares.

Within the proposed fundraising, which it wants to use to raise about 45 million stg, Biocompatibles expects to use about 35 million stg to help fund the new joint venture and its continuing development programe.
The remaining 10 million stg would fund "other new product development programmes in the cardiovascular field, in particular relating to stent grafts".
